related_work: Miguel talked about some important ideas. The McGurk effect shows that what we see can change what we hear. Kevin Donnelly said there are three levels: tight sync, half sync, and no sync. Michel Chion said that when sound and image happen at the same time, our brain joins them together, even if they don’t really belong together.
conclusion_future_work: I learned that sound is not just added to a picture. It changes how we feel and understand it. Next week, we will make a short animation, so I want to think about how sound can follow the picture or go against it. I also want to watch the films he suggested, like Sound of Metal and A Quiet Place.
results_discussion: We watched many film clips. In Star Wars, the spaceship sound is made from elephants and cars, but we believe it because it’s in sync. In Jaws, the music only plays when the shark is there. In Gravity, you only hear sound when the character touches something, so you feel like you are inside her body. Miguel’s own research found that in concert videos, the camera tells us which part of the music to listen to. If the camera cuts at the wrong time, the music feels broken.
title: week5
introduction: This week, Miguel Mera, a film composer, gave us a talk about sound and picture. The key word was “synchronisation”, which means how sound and image match. The talk also got us ready for next week’s animation class.
